about: ModelPilot's execution policy (switch_policy.py). Jev predicts the model and effort a task needs; ModelPilot switches there directly only when the expected total cost says it pays and, with quality_floor on, only among settings no worse than the user's own model. Models, efforts, cache behaviour and the cost model live here so they can change without code. Prices come from the rate files merged by bench.rates().

claude-haiku-5-5.not_a_session_setting: User decision, October 10: Haiku 5.5 is for helper roles (summaries, single simple steps inside larger tasks), not whole everyday tasks, so the policy never moves a session to it. As a candidate (October 9-10) it took every turn start of modelpilot-for-sonnet (runs/bench-20261010-090944, 29/29), on a measured rate from the 29 tuning tasks, which are too easy to separate the tiers (every tier passes about 26 of them every time). The measurements below stay for the helper roles; none is built yet.
claude-haiku-5-5.candidate_evidence: Replaced Haiku 4.5 on October 8 (Haiku 5.5, released October 7: cheaper per token at any prompt length; takes effort, adaptive thinking and Claude Code's mid-history system messages, which Haiku 4.5 rejected). A candidate since October 9 (user decisions: every arm, October 8, reached only by proxy moves from the client's Sonnet 5.5; its outcomes bound its own settings only, October 9). Measured on the 29 tuning tasks (runs/haiku-policy-evidence-20261008.json; runs/haiku-arms-analysis-20261008.json): at medium it meets the quality floor for a Sonnet 5.5 medium user, not for an Opus one; low concise doesn't, so candidate_efforts is the measured medium. Thinking history: Sonnet 5.5 -> Haiku 5.5, Haiku 5.5 -> Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku's own effort rung accepted in both shapes and repeats (runs/thinking-probe-haiku-5-5-20261009-124512, in THINKING_HISTORY_VERIFIED). Not probed: Haiku 5.5 <-> Opus 5.5 with thinking history.
claude-haiku-5-5.per_message_effort_evidence: The proxy move's effort check, verdict holds by the rule fixed before the run (thinking_probe.move_effort_verdict; runs/thinking-probe-haiku-effort-20261009-130808, 200 requests, $0.12): with the client's own low effort message in place, the proxy's later message for xhigh raised Haiku's thinking to 1,996 mean tokens a repeat, against 1,849 at native xhigh and 1,185 at the client's low (every repeat above every low repeat), the cache kept at every step. On these puzzles native medium thought only 1.06x low, so the xhigh pair decides; move_pm at medium read 1,324 against native medium's 1,260. The first run's move cases (runs/thinking-probe-haiku-5-5-20261009-124512) agreed but couldn't separate low from medium.
claude-haiku-5-5.effort_switch_evidence: With thinking, Haiku 5.5 effort changes (medium to high) read the tools and system (8,023-8,028 tokens, where the control read all 8,044-8,049) and rewrote only the messages, 4/4 (runs/thinking-probe-haiku-5-5-20261009-124512), as Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 do. Without thinking they read everything, 6/6 (runs/m0-replication-haiku-5-5-20261009-124740), as Opus 5.5's did; Claude Code's requests think. In the same cache run, moves to Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 wrote, returns to Haiku read their entry 12/12, and an entry lived the 5-minute sliding window (read at 240 s, written anew at 330 s).
claude-haiku-5-5.run_factor_evidence: Haiku 5.5 medium (client on Haiku 5.5, its own ~40 KB prompt) against Sonnet 5.5 at the client's medium on the same task, over the 29 tuning tasks (every recorded sonnet-5.5 fixed-arm trial; Haiku: bench-20261008-195122, bench-20261008-214840): 2.11x the main-loop requests and 2.32x the output per request (geometric means; per task 1.15-5.3x and 1.17-4.98x; runs/haiku-policy-evidence-20261008.json). Reached by a proxy move it gets Sonnet's ~11 KB prompt instead, unmeasured.

claude-sonnet-5-5.effort_switch_evidence: Sonnet 5.5 effort changes read the tools and system (7,871-7,873 tokens) and rewrote only the messages (465-504), 8/8 (runs/thinking-probe-sonnet-5-5-20260928-133426); Sonnet 5 had rewritten everything.

claude-opus-5-5.run_factor_evidence: Against Sonnet 5.5 on the same task, both at the client's medium, over the 23 tuning tasks of the fixed arms in bench-20260929-000001 and bench-20260930-161402: 1.25x the main-loop requests and 1.16x the output per request (geometric means).
claude-opus-5-5.effort_switch_evidence: Opus 5.5 effort changes kept tools and system cached and rewrote only the messages (runs/thinking-probe-opus-5-5-effort-20260926-132158).

effort_factor_evidence: Output per request and main-loop requests against medium on the same task. high: Sonnet 5.5 on the 4 tasks the ModelPilot arm ran at high in bench-20261003-095823 (with per-message effort, so the effort held) against fixed Sonnet 5.5 medium in bench-20260930-161402: 1.23x output, 1.33x requests (geometric means; 1.09-1.52 and 1.10-1.83). xhigh: one Opus 5.5 task (cachetools-cached-condition), against fixed Opus 5.5 medium: 1.23x output, 2.12x requests, applied to both models. low (October 6, runs/low-effort-factors-20261006.json, $0): Sonnet 5.5 low concise against Sonnet 5.5 concise (medium) on the 23 tuning tasks, the concise prompt the ModelPilot arms carry: 0.94x requests, 0.90x output per request (geometric means; 0.67-1.75 and 0.57-1.36); without the prompt, low against medium in bench-20261003-172258: 0.92x and 0.94x. It was a guess (1.0x requests, 0.7x output). max is an unmeasured guess (at least xhigh's). The earlier guesses (output only, high 1.6, xhigh 2.4) had no request factor.
defaults_evidence: The shape of a Sonnet 5.5 medium task, pooled over the 23 tuning tasks of fixed Sonnet 5.5 (bench-20260929-000001, bench-20260930-161402): 7.0 main-loop requests, 480 output tokens and 810 other new tokens written to the cache per request (rounded to 500 and 800). For a 7,100-token first request these defaults forecast $0.090 for Sonnet 5.5 medium and $0.218 for Opus 5.5 medium, against $0.085 and $0.219 measured per task (pooled); fed each task set's own measured shape, run_cost gives $0.072 and $0.126 against $0.069 and $0.121 for Sonnet, $0.175 and $0.315 against $0.170 and $0.333 for Opus. The earlier guesses (15 requests, 1,500 and 1,200 tokens) forecast about $0.30, 2.5-4x too high. All at Sonnet 5.5's $0.20 cache reads; since they fell to $0.10 on October 7 (forecasts use today's prices, cache_probe.dated) the Sonnet 5.5 medium forecast is $0.0825. Replayed, no recorded decision changes (runs/sonnet-reads-repriced-20261008.json).
bytes_per_token_evidence: Request JSON bytes per token of the first main-loop request: 2.77-2.85 (mean 2.82) over the 30 recorded turn-start decisions of bench-20260929-000001, bench-20261001-185542 and bench-20261003-095823. It was 4, which put prefixes about 30% low.
cache_lifetime_evidence: How long the setting just sent counts as warm, by the lifetime its request's breakpoints asked for (the client marks 5m with an API key, 1h on a subscription or with CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h; the write is then billed at write_1h). 5m: M0's sliding five minutes (runs/m0-ttl-20260921-202543; Opus 5.5: m0-replication-opus-5-5-20260924-214653). 1h: the API's nominal hour, unmeasured until the one-hour probe (plan item 6). Counting an entry warm when it has expired only makes a move look dearer than it is, so the nominal figure errs toward staying. Returns to an earlier setting's entry (return_reuse) still count only within cache_ttl_seconds.

recovery.wasted_evidence: October 4 (user request: price a failure as the realistic cost of redoing it): all 22 failed Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 trials on the tuning split (strict grading, every run through bench-20261004-195612) ended with the session reporting success, its fix in place; only Haiku's 2 failures hit the turn limit. So the whole run is spent before anyone notices, not half of it (0.5 before). The redo is a new session on a stronger model: on the 28 priced tuning tasks a cold Opus 5.5 run averages $0.25 (runs/redo-cost-20261004.json). Human time to notice the bug is not counted.
recovery.redo_on: Jev's recommendation when at least as strong as the failed setting and reachable, else the strongest reachable setting. A failure shows inside the turn, where the effort can't change (effort_changes_at), so reachable means a model at the failed setting's effort: Sonnet 5.5 medium is redone on Opus 5.5 medium, not Opus 5.5 max as before October 3.

exploration.about: Randomized mid-task switches, for measurement only (user request, October 7): the modelpilot-explore arm turns this on. Each trial draws, from a hash of its task, arm and trial number, whether it switches (with this probability) and at which main-loop request (uniform from first_request to last_request); at that request the policy moves to target_model at the turn's effort (effort can change only at turn starts), whatever the cost gate says, and journals the move (kind exploration) with the switch cost it predicted. Random assignment makes switched and unswitched trials comparable. No other move is made: the arm has no advisor.

hysteresis_scaling: A move must beat staying by hysteresis_usd x P(the current setting is enough): full protection for a plausible current setting, almost none for one that is nearly certain to fail.

step.about: Mid-task decision points (user request, September 29). A step is due when the host-run test suite flips between failing and passing (run_tests results in the ledger), or when the task's measured spend since the last decision reaches overrun_factor x that decision's forecast for the setting it kept or chose. It needs at least min_requests_between billable requests of the task since the last decision, and there are at most max_per_revision per task revision. Candidates are a turn start's plus Jev's effort on the current model, so an effort-only move is always weighed.

return_reuse.about: Price a move to a setting whose own cache entry is still warm (sent within cache_ttl_seconds) and within reach (the conversation has grown by at most max_positions content positions since that setting was last sent) as writing only what that entry doesn't cover. Measured with thinking history in the pinned client's shape (runs/thinking-probe-returns-20260930-091128, $0.4056): returns read the home setting's whole entry 8/8, Sonnet 5.5 effort returns 7 and 25 positions back and Opus 5.5 -> Sonnet 5.5 model returns 8 back. The API documents a 20-position lookback, yet 25 was reached; farther is unmeasured, so it is priced like a first switch.

per_message_effort.about: Effort rides in an effort-only system message (beta mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01; Claude Code 2.1.284 already sends its older spelling per-turn-control-2026-07-01) placed after the client's own effort message, which 2.1.284 puts on the system note after the prompt; the top-level effort stays the client's. Every earlier message is put back where it was first sent. Evidence (runs/thinking-probe-per-message-effort-20261001-160146, $0.93): a message at a turn start raised thinking to the native xhigh level at every step with the cache kept; changes inside the tool loop, by message or top-level, changed nothing and also kept the cache (the client's message outranks the top-level effort). So new messages are added only at turn starts (effort_changes_at).

delegation.about: Two more ways to act on Jev's advice mid-task, besides staying and switching (docs/m6-modelpilot-policy.md, 'Delegation'). Both are side requests the proxy sends itself, admitted and settled by the governor, and delivered into the main conversation as system-role text kept in place on every later request. Off in the modelpilot arm; the modelpilot-delegate arm turns them on.

consult.about: Consult Jev's model at Jev's effort on a bounded brief of host facts (task instruction, latest run_tests result, the agent's own test runs through Bash with the output the client returned, diff against the trial's base commit, why it is asking; test_output_bytes caps each of the two test sections), when that setting is stronger than the current one and the gate prices it below staying and switching. P_consult = P_ok(current) + effectiveness x (P_ok(target) - P_ok(current)); effectiveness, output_tokens (thinking included, at medium; scaled by the effort output factor) and advice_tokens are guesses. route_brief: Jev answers who takes the brief. force: step causes ('tests_now_pass', 'tests_now_fail', 'spend_overrun', 'tests_pass': the latest run_tests passes for the first time in the revision, or 'agent_finish': the agent ends its turn, held once per turn by the Stop hook so the review reaches it) at which a consult is made whatever its price, for measurement only.

handoff_note.about: Before a mid-task model switch (the request holds earlier assistant turns), the model being left writes a short state-of-the-work note in a side request that reuses its cache; the note goes into the new model's first request. Its cost (the prefix read, output_tokens including thinking, and note_tokens written into the new conversation) is added to the switch; its benefit is unmeasured and not priced.

calibration.evidence: Strict passes (the hidden grader and the task's whole edge suite; user decision, October 4) of the fixed arms over every full set of the 29 tuning tasks (the 6 networkx tasks since October 6; networkx became a tuning repository by user decision on October 4). Sonnet 5.5 medium 48/52: 16/16 in bench-20260929-000001, 6/7 in bench-20260930-161402, 21/23 in bench-20261003-172258 and 5/6 in the networkx screening bench-20261004-191238; the misses are tomli-decode-error-attrs twice, parse-decimal-grouping once and nx-ismags-monomorphism once. Opus 5.5 medium 29/29 (16/16, 7/7, 6/6). Sonnet 5.5 low (October 6, plan item 2) is sonnet-5.5-low-concise, the ModelPilot arms' start: 27/29, 21/23 in bench-20261003-210450 + bench-20261004-081527 (the rate-limited trial left out; misses tomli-decode-error-attrs and parse-decimal-grouping, as at medium) and 6/6 in bench-20261004-191238. Those arms carry the concise prompt in every setting; at medium it didn't change strict outcomes (sonnet-5.5-concise 21/23 in bench-20261003-194736, the same two misses), so the medium and Opus outcomes without it stand for those settings. Repeats of tasks Sonnet had missed are left out (bench-20261004-135219, bench-20261004-195612): they would bias the rates. With a uniform prior: Sonnet 5.5 low (27 + 1) / (29 + 2) = 0.903, medium (48 + 1) / (52 + 2) = 0.907, Opus 5.5 medium (29 + 1) / (29 + 2) = 0.968. A setting takes the highest rate among the measured settings it is at least as strong as, so Opus 5.5 low takes Sonnet 5.5 low's (unmeasured itself). Until October 6 the rates covered the first 23 tasks at medium only: Sonnet 43/46 (0.917), Opus 23/23 (0.96). On hidden tests alone Sonnet and Opus medium were both 0.96 (23/23 each in the first two runs). Haiku 5.5 (in since October 9, user decision): low 25/29 (haiku-5.5-low-concise, bench-20261008-195122) and medium 56/58 (haiku-5.5, bench-20261008-195122 and bench-20261008-214840, missing tomli-decode-error-attrs both times; runs/haiku-policy-evidence-20261008.json). They stand for Haiku's own settings only (its outcomes_count_for_stronger is false): Haiku 5.5 medium passed parse-decimal-grouping and nx-ismags-monomorphism on both trials, which Sonnet 5.5 medium missed, so its 56/58 doesn't raise Sonnet's or Opus's rates.
calibration.about: P_ok at turn starts and steps is (1 - jev_weight) x the measured pass rate of the strongest measured setting the candidate is at least as strong as (on the candidate's own model when the measured model's outcomes_count_for_stronger is false, as Haiku 5.5's is), plus jev_weight x Jev's estimate; a candidate with no measured setting at or below it keeps Jev's alone (Sonnet 5.5 low did until October 6; now every candidate has one). Jev's estimate read as given had put Sonnet 5.5 medium at 0.02-0.94 on those 23 tasks, all of which it passed on hidden tests. jev_weight is 0.03 since October 6: refitted the same way over all 110 calibration outcomes, with Sonnet 5.5 low's (runs/jev-weight-fit-20261006.json; posterior mean 0.028, 95% bound 0.08, maximum likelihood 0). Jev's effort answer almost never allows low (its mean estimate for Sonnet 5.5 low is 0.01 over the 29 tasks, where low concise passed 27), so at 0.09 the gate left the low start for Sonnet 5.5 medium at 37 of 83 recorded turn starts, a move that costs more at the same measured pass rate; at 0.06 or less every one stays (runs/policy-replay-low-concise-start-20261006.json). Alone, low's outcomes give 0.053 (bound 0.144), medium's 0.089 (0.237), Opus's 0.073 (0.214). From October 4 to 6 it was 0.09, the posterior mean on medium's outcomes below; before that 0.2, a judgment. With failures priced at their realistic redo cost (wasted_fraction 1.0), 0.2 jumped (runs/policy-replay-redo-weight-0.2-20261004.json) to Sonnet 5.5 high on parse-strftime-directives' two recorded turn starts, a task Sonnet 5.5 medium passed strictly in every trial; at 0.15 or less nothing jumps, and at 0.09 all 30 turn starts stay at Sonnet 5.5 medium (runs/policy-replay-redo-fitted-20261004.json). Under strict passes (October 4) Sonnet 5.5 medium missed 3 of 46 outcomes, at Jev estimates of 0.56 (tomli-decode-error-attrs, twice) and 0.80 (parse-decimal-grouping), while the tasks Jev rated lowest (0.02, 0.11, 0.11) passed: its warnings don't predict the misses. A uniform prior on jev_weight over those 46 outcomes (Jev's mean first turn-start answer per task) gives a posterior mean of 0.09, a 95% upper bound of 0.25 and a maximum-likelihood value of 0 (in-sample: the same outcomes set the measured rate; 0.14 and 0.38 over the first 23 alone), so 0.2 left Jev more weight than the outcomes support. Replayed with these outcomes (runs/policy-replay-strict-20261004.json), 0.2 keeps all 30 recorded turn starts at Sonnet 5.5 medium, as with hidden-test outcomes (runs/policy-replay-calibrated-20261003.json, where 0.25 jumped on 2 and 0.35 on 10). On stuck evidence Jev's estimate is used uncalibrated, conditioned on the current setting failing, since the measured rates can't say which setting rescues a task.

quality_floor.about: User decision, October 8: ModelPilot promises quality no worse than the user's own model (baseline) instead of pricing a miss, whose cost varies too much by change for one figure. A setting may be used when it is at least as strong as the baseline, or when, over at least min_shared_tasks tuning tasks measured for both, it missed no task the baseline never missed (a miss: any complete trial that failed strict grading). A setting takes the outcomes of the strongest measured setting it is at least as strong as (as P_ok does); the baseline takes those of the weakest measured setting at least as strong as it, or, with none, is taken to miss nothing. A move to a setting at least as strong as the current one is always allowed, so escalations, rescues and redos are never blocked. When the current setting is below the floor (at a turn start or step), the policy moves to the allowed setting with the lowest expected cost on measured pass rates, without asking Jev; if none is reachable (inside a turn the effort holds) it stays and says so. Among allowed settings the expected-cost rule decides as before. Off in the modelpilot arm; modelpilot-for-sonnet and modelpilot-for-opus turn it on with their baselines.
quality_floor.evidence: Per-task strict outcomes of the same trials as calibration.outcomes (runs/quality-floor-outcomes-20261008.py -> .json); load() checks that their totals equal the calibration's. Over the same 29 tuning tasks, Sonnet 5.5 low concise missed parse-decimal-grouping and tomli-decode-error-attrs, Sonnet 5.5 medium those two and nx-ismags-monomorphism, Opus 5.5 medium none. So against Sonnet 5.5 medium every Sonnet 5.5 setting is allowed, low included; against Opus 5.5 medium none is, until per-task evidence (plan items 8 and 10) says which tasks are safe. min_shared_tasks is a judgment: fewer shared tasks are too little to call a setting no worse. That a stronger setting is never worse is assumed, not measured. Haiku 5.5's outcomes (since October 9) bound only Haiku's settings (outcomes_count_for_stronger false, as in the calibration): against Sonnet 5.5 medium, Haiku 5.5 medium is allowed (its one miss, tomli-decode-error-attrs, Sonnet medium makes too) and low isn't (it adds nx-classes-weak-views); against Opus 5.5 medium neither is.

measured_candidates.about: User decision, October 8: at a turn start every runnable setting with measured tuning outcomes (calibration.outcomes) is weighed beside Jev's pick, on the same expected cost, whether or not Jev names it: Jev's weight is 0.03 because it doesn't predict the misses, so the candidates it names shouldn't decide which measured settings are weighed. A measured candidate Jev didn't name may be a downgrade without Jev's confidence (its evidence is the measured rate), but pays the downgrade's extra hysteresis. Without Jev's answer nothing moves (advice_unavailable), as before; the gate prices these candidates too, so it asks Jev wherever a move could pay. Replayed over the recorded runs before it was turned on: runs/measured-candidates-replay-20261008.json.

jev_gate.about: Plan item 1 (October 6): Jev is asked only where some answer it could give changes the decision. Its choices and confidences pick the candidates; its probabilities only set each setting's estimate, in [0, 1]. With a failure wasting its whole run (recovery.wasted_fraction 1), every expected cost falls as any P_ok rises, so switch_policy.jev_gate bounds each answer shape (each model and effort choice, sure or unsure of each, or no effort answer) by staying with Jev's estimate 0 against each candidate with 1. If no candidate beats staying by the hysteresis even then, Jev isn't called and the decision is journaled as a stay (jev_cannot_change). Never at uncalibrated points (stuck evidence) or where a consult is possible, whose target is Jev's setting. Replayed over the seven ModelPilot runs (runs/policy-replay-jev-gate-20261006.json): all 180 recorded decisions skip Jev at jev_weight 0.03, none moves on its real answer; from 0.06 every turn start asks.

guesses: The max effort factor, hysteresis_usd, downgrade_switch_multiplier, the step spacing, cap and overrun factor, and quality_floor.min_shared_tasks are starting values, not measurements. The defaults, bytes_per_token, the low, high and xhigh effort factors, the model factors, the calibration outcomes, jev_weight and recovery.wasted_fraction are measured or fitted (see their evidence), on few tasks.
